  "output_head": "# Chat Bots Architecture

## Data Model
Bots are `User` records with `role: :bot` (`User::Role`), implemented via the `User::Bot` concern:
- `users.bot_token`: unique random token (`SecureRandom.base58(24)`) generated on create for bots; `nil` for human users and deactivated bots.
- `users.creator_id`: references the `User` who created the bot, allowing `Current.user.can_administer?(bot)` to work uniformly for creators and administrators.
- `users.webhook_url`: optional HTTP/HTTPS URL where the bot receives webhook callbacks. Blank values normalize to `nil` so clearing the field removes the webhook.
- `users.add_to_all_open_rooms`: boolean (default `false`). Bots do not join open rooms by default; when enabled, the bot is added to all existing open rooms and automatically joins any open room created or converted from closed later. Disabling it keeps existing memberships.
- `bot_key` (`"<id>-<bot_token>"`): the credential displayed in the UI ("Bot code") and used in the messaging API URL. Verified with `ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare`.
- Reusing `User` means bots automatically inherit:
  - Opt-in open-room auto-join (`User#grant_membership_to_open_rooms` and `Rooms::Open` via `User.open_room_members`)
  - Closed-room membership management (`Rooms::ClosedsController`)
  - `@`-mention autocompletion (`Autocompletable::UsersController`) and `Message#mentionees` resolution
  - Message authorship (`messages.creator_id`), avatars (`User::Avatar`), broadcasts (`Message::Broadcasts`), and push notifications (`Room::MessagePusher`)
- Bots are excluded from human-only surfaces (login, session transfers, account member list, sidebar DM placeholders) via `User.not_bot`.
- Deleting a bot calls `User#deactivate`, which sets `status: :deactivated`, clears `bot_token: nil`, `webhook_url: nil`, and `add_to_all_open_rooms: false`, and removes all memberships while preserving historical messages.

## Routes & Controllers
- `BotsController` (`resources :bots, except: :show`): UI for listing (`/bots`), creating (`/bots/new`), editing (`/bots/:id/edit`), and deleting bots. Linked from `/account/edit` ("Set up chat bots") for all members. The form includes the optional `Webhook URL` field (`bot[webhook_url]`) and the `Add to all open rooms` switch (`bot[add_to_all_open_rooms]`).
- `Bots::MessagesController` (`POST /rooms/:room_id/:bot_key/messages`): unauthenticated, CSRF-exempt endpoint reading raw request body (or `params[:attachment]`) and returning `201 Created` with `Location: /messages/:message_id`, `422 Unprocessable Content`, `404 Not Found`, or `401 Unauthorized`.

## Outbound Webhooks (`Bot::Webhook` & `Bot::WebhookJob`)
- `mention` event: When a message is created (`after_create_commit -> { room.receive(self) }`), `Room#deliver_bot_webhooks_later` finds active, mentioned bots in that room that have a `webhook_url` (excluding `message.creator`) and enqueues one `Bot::WebhookJob` per bot.
  - Payload: `{ event: "mention", author: { id, name }, room: { id, name, reply_to }, message: { id, body: { text, html }, link } }`.
  - `message.body.text` strips only the target bot's own `<action-text-attachment>` mention node(s) using a unique sentinel before converting to plain text, handling both ASCII spaces and ` ` (`\u00A0`) while preserving other users' and bots' `@`-mentions.
- `joined` event: All membership insertions go through `Membership.grant`, which uses `insert_all(..., returning: %i[ room_id user_id ])` so only newly created memberships (never duplicates or already-existing memberships) trigger `Bot::WebhookJob` (`enqueue_after_transaction_commit = true`) for active bots with a `webhook_url` in non-direct rooms (`Room.without_directs`). Direct rooms (`Rooms::Direct`) never trigger `joined`.
  - Payload: `{ event: "joined", room: { id, name, reply_to } }` (`reply_to` is the relative `room_bot_messages_path` for that room & bot).
- Enqueueing per-bot background jobs ensures webhook HTTP calls never block the user or delay other bots.
- Synchronous responses for both `mention` and `joined`:
  - `200` with `text/plain` (HTML-escaped so literal text renders safely) or `text/html` posts the non-blank response body into the room as the bot's message and calls `broadcast_create`.
  - `204` (or other statuses / empty body) posts nothing.
- Outbound webhook URLs intentionally permit `http://` and `https://` on localhost and private networks (unlike `Opengraph::Fetch`) so self-hosted Campfire instances and local integrations/tests can target internal services.

    @room  = Rooms::Closed.new(name: DEFAULT_ROOM_NAME)
    @users = User.active.ordered
  end

  def create
    room = Rooms::Closed.create_for(room_params, users: grantees)

    broadcast_create_room(room)
    redirect_to room_url(room)
  end

  def edit
    selected_user_ids = @room.users.pluck(:id)
    @selected_users, @unselected_users = User.active.ordered.partition { |user| selected_user_ids.include?(user.id) }
  end

  def update
    @room.update! room_params
    @room.memberships.revise(granted: grantees, revoked: revokees)

    broadcast_update_room
    redirect_to room_url(@room)
  end

    def force_room_type
      @room = @room.becomes!(Rooms::Closed)
    end

    # Open and closed rooms convert into each other, so both are in reach here. Direct
    # rooms never are: converting one would let its creator revise who's in it.
    def room_scope
      Current.user.rooms.without_directs
    end

      User.where(id: grantee_ids)
    end

    def revokees
      @room.users.where.not(id: grantee_ids)
    end

      params.fetch(:user_ids, [])
